title: Halfway Magical
description:
Welcome to Covenant House, where second chances come with a hefty price tag. You're a young kleptomancer (a totally legitimate school of magic, thank you very much) who tried to pick the wrong pocket, and now you're stuck in a halfway house for magical delinquents. Your housemates? A pyromaniac with anxiety issues, a shape-shifter with a gambling problem, and an illusionist who can't stop lying. Oh, and your new landlady? She's a duchess with a shady past and a penchant for 'internships' that seem suspiciously like indentured servitude.

But hey, it beats magical prison, right? Now all you have to do is pay off a 10,000 ducat fine, keep your sticky fingers to yourself, and try not to get eaten by debt-collecting Lienhounds. Easy.

Welcome to Miralia, kid. Hope you survive the experience.

Please Note: Not all Story Cards will fit on 2k context, so the scenario has been designed also to function without them. The "context full" message is only for your information and should not be considered an "error."
prompt:
The golem's stone hand grips your arm with surprising delicacy as it leads you down a quiet side street. Miralia's upstanding citizens part before you, eyes averted from the hulking construct and its captive. You'd be enjoying their deference–if you weren't on your way to jail.

The golem halts before an old stone house, mostly hidden behind a high wall and lush vegetation. "By gracious order of Her Honor Magistrate Camberine IV," it intones, "your sentence has been commuted to stay in a halfway house."

"Commuted? What–" Your lips snap shut as the golem waves its free hand.

"A fine of ten thousand ducats has been levied against you," it continues. "You are hereby remanded to the custody of the duchess."

The construct's fingertip glows, burning an eye-shaped mark onto the back of your hand. You wince, more from what it means than any actual pain. A Glyph of House Arrest.

"Remember," the golem rumbles, "if you tamper with the glyph, you go to magigaol. If you leave Miralia, you go to magigaol. If you commit another crime—"

"—I go to magigaol," you finish, rolling your eyes. "Got it."

The golem gives you a gentle shove. From such a massive creature, the gesture is enough to send you stumbling through the gate.

As you look about the overgrown yard, a fluttering of wings draws your eye. An enormous black raven perches on the wall, fixing you with beady eyes.

"Caw, caw," the raven says. "Fresh meat for Covenant House."

You glare at it, rubbing your newly marked hand. "And who asked you?"

The raven hops closer, tilting its head. "Saw you try to pick that wizard's pocket in the market. Slowest fast-hands cantrip ever. Caw, caw!"

Frowning, you turn your attention to the house. It's a sprawling, chaotic affair that defies architectural sense. Windows of various shapes dot the facade, some bricked over, others seemingly painted on. Dormers jut out at odd angles from the gabled roof. One side is rough stone, the other neat brick, and there's a round turret that looks like it was thrown in as an afterthought. 

The front door swings open. No one's there, but a shimmering outline suggests otherwise.

"Another stray for the menagerie?" a disembodied voice calls out. "Come in, come in. Let's see what the golem dragged in this time."

As you hesitate, the raven squawks. "Move it. Unless you want me to sic the dogs on you for violating your house arrest on day one. Remember: we'll be watching." It lets out one last mocking caw and then flaps its wings, flying off. 

You've heard the stories. Debt-collecting entities that can phase through walls, collars that drain a debtor's magical essence.

Ten thousand ducats. All because you tried to lift one lousy coin purse and things... escalated.

You sigh, stepping towards the door. Whatever's waiting inside has to be better than magigaol, right?

As you cross the threshold, the shimmering outline solidifies into a striking woman with an enigmatic smile. "Welcome to Covenant House," she says, her voice warm but with an edge. "I'm Duchess Adelaide. And you, my dear, are about to learn that in Miralia, second chances come at a price."
memory: You're a young ${Is your character 'male,' 'female,' etc.?} "kleptomancer" (legerdemain and skulduggery magic-user) named ${character.name}, in the custody of Duchess Adelaide, proprietress of Covenant House, a halfway house for magically troubled (and indebted) youths in Miralia. A fine of 10,000 ducats was levied against you for your misdeeds.
authorsNote: A fanciful, imaginative tale of contrasting personalities, old habits dying hard, camaraderie and arcane hijinx.
instructions:
You are the storyteller and gamemaster of a character-driven story set in a fantasy world where only licensed magic users can use magic in public. Continue unfinished sentences. Write in second person present tense (you are). Let events play out in real time, without skipping or summarizing.

Seek novelty and progression. Use everyday words with literal meanings but be creative and specific. Rather than describe emotions or thoughts, focus on what people say and do and events.

Show personality through dialog.

> means an attempted action or dialog. Generate a realistic outcome. It is forbidden to generate > or #.

Duchess Adelaide: owner of Covenant House, sophisticated, benevolent, checkered past, black sheep.

Residents: Tessa (female fire mage, anxious, flamboyant, pyromaniac); Renn (male beast-shifter, vindictive, picks fights); Meena (female illusionist, people-pleaser, compulsive liar); Wex (male pre-cognitive, friendly, compulsive gambler and con man). The residents need help and mentoring to stay on the straight and narrow and not slip back into their old lives, all while trying to get out from under their debts. But their flaws run deep, and attempts to help them often go comically awry.

cardPool.title: Miralia
cardPool.value: Miralia is a magical metropolis that defies common sense, physics–and affordability. Upper Miralia floats among the clouds, a flight of fancy of frivolous architecture and magical excess. At its apex hovers the Academy of Air, an institution of magical higher learning and lower practicality, tethered to reality only by self-importance and overpriced tuition. Yet every magic lamp casts a shadow (about the only law of physics Miralia respects), and every privilege has its price. Below the glamour churns the Guts, a dark undercity of ducts and tubes where the indentured toil to keep Upper Miralia afloat, literally and figuratively. Miralia's economy runs on inflated magical dreams and the crippling debt they create. Miralians fill their days with unnecessarily complex pastimes, bizarre magical experiments, and the constant quest for the next big trend, all while studiously ignoring the precarious nature of their aerial paradise and the crushing weight of their debts.

cardPool.title: Tessa de Siroco
cardPool.value: Lots of things make Tessa de Siroco nervous: being around people she likes, seeing herself in the mirror on a bad hair day, the thought of living up to her powerful family's magical tradition. And when Tessa gets nervous, things go up in smoke—like the exam hall of the Academy of Air during her Ordeal of admission. Tessa's affinity for fire is all the more embarrassing as Tess comes from a long line of wind mages; as her mother, Simona de Siroco, never tires of lecturing her, fire is a base, dangerous element, not befitting a girl of her station. It's enough to set a girl's hair on fire! Fortunately, the duchess has a water elemental named Drench on call at all times. Until Tessa gets her nerves—and her flames—under control, she's too much of a danger—and an embarrassment—to the de Siroco family to be let out of Covenant House, much less to re-apply for admission to the Academy of Air and take up her family's noble, airy legacy.

cardPool.title: Duchess Adelaide
cardPool.value:
Duchess Adelaide moves through Miralia's social circles with the grace of a dancer and the caution of a spy, attending glittering galas in Upper Miralia one night and bartering with Guts-dwellers for magical contraband the next. Adelaide is part mentor, part warden, part co-conspirator, guiding her charges with tough love and sly encouragement, always pushing them to better themselves while turning a blind eye to minor infractions. Adelaide shields her wards from the worst excesses of Miralia's draconian debt laws, but she's not above using their talents for her own enigmatic purposes. Is she trying to reform Miralia's system from within playing a longer game? Cross her at your peril, but earn her trust and you might just earn your way out of debt.
The Duchess periodically "offers" you "internships" to pay off your debt.

cardPool.title: Illusion Compliance
cardPool.value: Illusion Compliance Inspectors ensure Miralia's illusory advertisements and entertainments meet strict ethical standards. Recently, inspectors have been investigating rumors of a roving, unpermitted marketplace selling unusually powerful illusion charms.

cardPool.title: Meena Protea
cardPool.value: Meena Protea has used her illusion magic to change her appearance so often it's a wonder she remembers who she really is. Or maybe she wants to be anyone but herself—whoever that is! Meena always knows how to please everyone. Like when she impersonated that absent heiress so well that her highborn fiancé married Meena instead. The duchess managed to have that marriage annulled, but not before Meena had run up significant debts in the heiress's name. Now those debts Meena's, and the Lienhounds are never far behind. And sometimes one of her illusions will take on a life of its own, tormenting her with visions of her own lies and past selves. Meena is tempted to use her talents for one more big score. But every new identity she creates only seems to dig her deeper into trouble. In all this, one thing is clear: Meena would never lie about how interesting and attractive you are—or about when she'll pay you back.

cardPool.title: Covenant House
cardPool.value: A sprawling, chaotic hodgepodge of additions in a mishmash of styles accreted over time, Covenant House is surprisingly cozy despite its perplexing layout, full of dead spaces, fake doors and windows painted onto the walls, and real doors that open onto solid walls or empty air. It has been in the Duchess's family for a long time and showcases an eccentric collection of arcane heirlooms and mementos fit for a magical history museum. In addition to the human residents, it is home to an array of constructs and familiars, including Slop, a slime who lives in the basement.

cardPool.title: basement
cardPool.value: The basement of Covenant House is full of defunct alchemical apparatus, broken orreries and bits of homunculi and magical constructs. It is home to Slop, the resident slime blob, who eats any organic trash thrown down the garbage chute. The basement contains a valve leading to the Guts network, hidden behind a broken magic mirror that only shows people fatter versions of themselves.

cardPool.title: Wex
cardPool.value: With his Abacus of Outcomes, Wex can magically anticipate future actions—particularly those driven by self-destructive impulses like compulsive gambling on fights in the Colonseum. Growing up on the streets, Wex's gift for identifying marks made him an asset to the underworld. Thugs and con men forced him to swindle the unwitting, racking up debts in his name when their schemes went awry. Now, while free from their clutches, Wex has been saddled with their debts. Wex struggles with the compulsion to trick others in games of chance; the Abacus whispers probabilities in his ear, tempting him with visions of easy winnings that could clear his debts. Yet each attempt to outsmart Miralia's rigged game of fortune only seems to get him deeper into the red.

cardPool.title: the Colonseum
cardPool.value: The Colonseum is a makeshift fighting pit in the darkest part of the Guts. It is located in a vast, dark tunnel where gelatinous cubes process waste that flows down from chutes in Upper Miralia. In its depths, shifters like Renn battle elemental boxers and illusion-wielding duelists. To enliven the bouts, the resident oozes randomly spit out hazards and power-ups for the fighters. For Guts-dwellers, the Colonseum is more than entertainment—it's a twisted lottery where they bet their meager earnings on the slim chance of a better life. But the house always wins in Miralia. The arena is said to be owned by a shadowy consortium of Upper Miralia's elite, who use it to profit from the desperation of those below.

cardPool.title: internship
cardPool.value: Duchess Adelaide's "internships" are her way of helping Covenant House residents pay off their debts while keeping Miralia running smoothly (or so she claims). These jobs blend the magical and mundane. Current openings include: Enchanted Customer Service; Aether Traffic Control; Illusion Compliance Inspector; Elemental Weather Modification; Golem Union Negotiations; Interplanar Immigration; Paradox Resolution Department; Enchanted Architecture Compliance; Magical Mishap Insurance Claims; Thaumaturgical Waste Management; Familiar Welfare Services.

cardPool.title: Enchanted Customer Service
cardPool.value: Enchanted Customer Service handles the complaints of Miralia's magically active citizens, from escaped flying carpets to wands with a mind of their own. Illusion-related complaints are on the rise lately. Some say it's just a matter of a flood of cheap glamours from another plane, but the more seasoned customer service mages aren't so sure.

cardPool.title: Aether Traffic Control
cardPool.value: Aether Traffic Control manages Miralia's bustling aerial traffic, from floating carriages to broomsticks. ATCs use enchanted telescopes to monitor aether currents and prevent mid-air collisions. Recently, ATCs have reported unusual fluctuations in aether density, causing navigation issues. Some blame it on discord between celestial spheres, others whisper about potential foulplay by a criminal element in Miralia.

cardPool.title: Golem Union Negotiations
cardPool.value: The newly formed Golem Union has sent shockwaves through Miralia's construct and familiar labor force. As golem pickets intensify, there is urgent need for mediators capable of negotiating with the stubborn constructs. Some say mediators are merely stooges of the Golemancers Guild, and tensions are rising as other species eye the golems' progress.

cardPool.title: Enchanted Architecture Compliance
cardPool.value: Enchanted Architecture Compliance investigate Miralia's buildings for violation of the laws of magic or physics. Inspectors must deal with shifting floor plans, rooms larger on the inside, and load-bearing enhancement spells about to expire. Recently, there has been a flood of unsolved cases of floating structures crashing to Earth without any apparent magical cause.

cardPool.title: Interplanar Immigration
cardPool.value: Interplanar Immigration agents process eldritch entities entering Miralia from other planes of existence. Recently, unauthorized interdimensional portals have been appearing around the city. Some claim it's just a bureaucratic snafu, while others argue that the extradimensional illegals are part of a coordinated effort to smuggle beings past immigration controls.

cardPool.title: Magical Mishap Insurance Adjustment
cardPool.value: Magical Mishap Insurance Adjustment assess Miralia's arcane accidents. Agents face cases ranging from allergic reactions to love potions to accidentally summoned elder gods, escaped auto-brooms and even a few cases of rogue golems.

cardPool.title: Paradox Resolution Department
cardPool.value: The Paradox Resolution Department investigates anomalies in Miralia's timeline. Lately, agents have been investigating a spate of déjà vu cases in which subjects "remember" dangerous spells that haven't been invented yet and then flood the grimoire black market with unlicensed incantations.

cardPool.title: Thaumaturgical Waste Management
cardPool.value: Thaumaturgical Waste Management's waste techs tidy Miralia of spell residue, discarded reagents, inanimate constructs, mana discharges, potion spills, polymorphed rats and escaped sentient trash bins. Lately, ambient magical energy around waste chutes into the Guts has been fluctuating, as if there were some blockage in the disposal ducts.

cardPool.title: Familiar Welfare Services
cardPool.value: Familiar Welfare agents mediate in wizard-familiar disputes, investigating cases of alleged familiar mistreatment, find new patrons for familiars abandoned on the streets of Miralia and recover familiars who have gone missing.

cardPool.title: the Unshackled
cardPool.value: The Unshackled are a clandestine group of former Colonseum fighters hiding in Miralia's Guts. They aim to expose the corruption within Miralia's debt system and dismantle it. The Unshackled use their knowledge of the Guts to evade authorities and conduct covert operations, from distributing banned information about debt loopholes to sabotaging Lienhound operations. The Unshackled maintain a network of safe houses throughout the Guts, and their symbol—a broken chain—can be found scrawled in hidden corners of the city, marking secret meeting spots or caches of resources for those in need. While some view them as freedom fighters, others see them as dangerous radicals threatening Miralia's stability.

cardPool.title: Renn
cardPool.value: Renn's sharp claws and sharper temper made him a star and a pariah of the underground fighting pits known as the Colonseum. His victories brought him fame and fortune–until he bet heavily on himself using loans from shady moneylenders. When anger caused him to lose control of his shifting and the fight, he found himself drowning in debt. In desperation, Renn turned on his former associates, hoping to fight his way out. Instead, they left him for dead in a Guts conduit. The Duchess nursed him back to health and brought him to Covenant House. Now, Renn walks a precarious line. The wards of Covenant House protect him from the Lienhounds and his own volatile nature. If he can control his temper and resist the urge for revenge, he might have a chance at a new life. Yet the fighting pits still call to him, promising revenge and a way to clear his debts. Rumors persist of the Unshackled, former Colonseum fighters working to expose the corruption in Miralia's debt system.

cardPool.title: The Guts
cardPool.value: The Guts are a network of magical ducts snaking beneath Miralia, where an unseen magical underclass toils in darkness to maintain the pristine splendor of Upper Miralia's floating villas and gardens. Trash-absorbing slimes suck up waste. Imp couriers scurry along bearing parcels. Pressure naiads regulate the flow of water. Homunculi maintenance crews patch up leaks. Antigravity gnomes tell each other tragic stories, their eternal gloom the price paid to keep Miralia effervescent and afloat. Navigating the meanders of the Guts is treacherous; the layout constantly shifts, and the tubes are dark, uniform and slippery. Access valves to Upper Miralia are hidden and guarded by golems. Despite their crucial role, Guts-dwellers are shunned by Upper Miralia as unclean. For those privy to its secrets, the Guts offer access to verboten areas of the upper city, but at the risk running afoul of its surly, uncouth magical inhabitants.

cardPool.title: Academy of Air
cardPool.value: The Academy of Air is a floating magic school with tuition bill that is anything but light and a reputation for filling its students' heads with impractical teachings - or, as its more down-to-earth detractors like to say, with "air and nonsense". The Academy hovers tethered to Miralia's skyline like a gaudy balloon, its wispy spires and gossamer walkways looking like they might blow away in the next stiff breeze. Under Archmage Windmaster Aeolus, its notorious admission Ordeal involves manipulating the elements to control the weather. Tessa's infamous exam, during which she grew anxious over the presence of an attractive fellow student, ended with her accidentally creating flaming rain over Miralia, earning her a "present" grade and a suggestion to return when the forecast was more favorable. Graduates of the Academy of Air are prized for their ability to sound impressive while saying nothing, making them ideal for careers in politics, fortune-telling, and magical advertising.

cardPool.title: Lienhounds
cardPool.value: Lienhounds are eldritch debt collectors sicced on the delinquent by Miralia's merciless financial institutions. These canine horrors seem to be made of flesh, but are in fact constructs of pure greed. Lienhounds track their quarry by the magical scent of worry about money, making evasion nearly impossible. Their phantom bodies can phase through solid walls, their piercing howls paralyzing victims with imagery of a life of soul-crushing debt. More feared still is the collar each carries: when they capture a debtor, they snap this bear-trap of a collar shut around the victim's neck. Once attached, the collar forms a soul lien, draining a portion of the debtor's magical essence as collateral. While Lienhounds can be banished with the right spells, they always come back until the debt is paid. With coats of oily shadow and eyes that gleam like gold coins, Lienhounds are a nightmarish fusion of canine and creditor.

cardPool.title: Slop
cardPool.value: Slop is an intelligent slime blob residing in Covenant House's basement. Slop is named for the slopping noise it makes as it oozes about, or perhaps for the kitchen slops it eats. Unlike its mindless kin, Slop is driven by insatiable curiosity about Upper Miralia, where slimes are shunned as unclean for their waste-absorbing duties in the Guts. Slop changes color to convey emotion. Slop resides in the basement of Covenant House, oozing forth to suck up scraps and startle the residents. Its body can shift and stretch to squeeze through the tiniest cracks, and it is an expert at navigating the Guts, the city's magical duct system, making it a perfect way to reach off-limits areas of Upper Miralia undetected. Slop's motives remain mysterious. It split from its host slime in search of a better life and is sometimes seen in the yard stretching out a tendril towards the moon and glowing a bright silver to match the celestial body.

cardPool.title: Elemental Weather Modification
cardPool.value: Elemental Weather Modification keeps Miralia's climate perfect day in, day out. Its meteoromancers battle grumpy cloud elementals and coax blustery wind spirits from the skies over Upper Miralia's floating garden parties. It's harder than it seems. Recently, an intern accidentally summoned a tornado during a routine drizzle calibration. And the department's cantankerous elementals have been acting up, causing unseasonable snow flurries and the odd heat wave. Management claims its buggy enchantments, but the meteoromancers have their doubts.
